patterns.en: Go ahead and unwrap your gift.
patterns.rule: Use the phrasal verb 'go ahead' to encourage someone to proceed; use the imperative mood for commands or suggestions.

patterns.en: Half of the students are absent.
patterns.rule: Use 'half of' + plural noun + plural verb; 'are' agrees with 'students'.

patterns.en: Give me a sip of your drink.
patterns.rule: Use the imperative form 'give' for requests; use possessive 'your' to indicate ownership.

patterns.en: I happen to be in love with you.
patterns.rule: Use 'happen to be' + adjective to indicate something is true by chance.

patterns.en: Don't hesitate to ask if you want anything.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't hesitate to' + base verb to encourage someone; use 'if' to introduce a condition.

patterns.en: Clearly, that was a mistake.
patterns.rule: Use 'clearly' to emphasize that something is obvious; past simple 'was' for past events.

patterns.en: I'm impressed with your French.
patterns.rule: Use 'be impressed with' + noun to express admiration.

patterns.en: I actually feel sorry for Tom.
patterns.rule: Use 'actually' to express a contrast or emphasize; present simple 'feel' for current feelings.

patterns.en: I'm beginning to understand why Tom loves Boston.
patterns.rule: Use 'be beginning to' + base verb to express a gradual realization.

patterns.en: In all probability, we'll arrive before them.
patterns.rule: Use 'in all probability' to express likelihood; 'will' + base verb for future actions.

patterns.en: I finally found my keys.
patterns.rule: Use 'finally' to indicate that something happened after a delay; past simple 'found' for completed action.

patterns.en: That's the reason I'm here.
patterns.rule: Use 'that's the reason' + clause to explain purpose; 'I'm' as a contraction of 'I am'.

patterns.en: I'm allergic to cigarette smoke.
patterns.rule: Use 'be allergic to' + noun to express medical conditions.

patterns.en: To be honest, I don't understand it.
patterns.rule: Use 'to be honest' to preface a frank statement; 'don't understand' in present simple for current states.

patterns.en: I've been studying French since I was 13.
patterns.rule: Use present perfect continuous ('have been' + verb-ing) for actions that started in the past and continue now; use 'since' + past time point.

patterns.en: For some reason, I'm wide awake and can't fall asleep.
patterns.rule: Use 'for some reason' to express an unknown cause; 'wide awake' as an adjective meaning fully awake.

patterns.en: In general, kids like ice cream.
patterns.rule: Use 'in general' to make generalizations; present simple for habitual actions.

patterns.en: Even if I knew, I wouldn't tell you.
patterns.rule: Use 'even if' + past tense to express a hypothetical condition; 'wouldn't' + base verb for unreal situations.

patterns.en: In fact, I don't think that was Tom.
patterns.rule: Use 'in fact' to emphasize a point; past simple 'was' for past identity.

patterns.en: Anyway, it's my problem.
patterns.rule: Use 'anyway' to change the topic or conclude; 'it's' as a contraction for 'it is'.

patterns.en: I'm looking for an apartment to rent.
patterns.rule: Use 'be looking for' + noun to express searching; 'to' + base verb to indicate purpose.

patterns.en: That's how it worked.
patterns.rule: Use 'that's how' + clause to explain a process; past simple 'worked' for completed actions.

patterns.en: For a moment, it looked like Tom might start crying.
patterns.rule: Use 'for a moment' to indicate a brief time; 'looked like' + clause to express appearance.

patterns.en: I can't tell you how much I appreciate your help.
patterns.rule: Use 'can't tell you how much' to emphasize gratitude.

patterns.en: I don't mind sleeping on the couch.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't mind' + verb-ing to express willingness to do something.

patterns.en: I don't believe Tom can do that.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't believe' + clause to express doubt; 'can' + base verb for ability.

patterns.en: I encourage Tom to learn French.
patterns.rule: Use 'encourage' + object + 'to' + base verb to motivate someone.

patterns.en: I especially like your chocolate cake.
patterns.rule: Use 'especially' to emphasize preference; present simple 'like' for habitual actions.

patterns.en: At one time, there was a bridge here.
patterns.rule: Use 'at one time' to refer to the past; 'there was' for singular past existence.

patterns.en: I suppose I should congratulate you.
patterns.rule: Use 'suppose' + clause to express tentative thoughts; 'should' + base verb for suggestions.

patterns.en: You have a good memory.
patterns.rule: Use present simple 'have' for possession.

patterns.en: Don't make fun of old people.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't make fun of' + noun to advise against mocking.

patterns.en: I didn't want to make the same mistake twice.
patterns.rule: Use past simple 'didn't want' for past desires; 'to make' + noun phrase to indicate the action.

patterns.en: By the way, where are you from?
patterns.rule: Use 'by the way' to introduce a new topic; 'are you' in question form for 'where' questions.

patterns.en: At least no one was hurt.
patterns.rule: Use 'at least' to indicate a minimum positive outcome; past simple 'was' for past state.

patterns.en: At this time, you don't need to understand everything.
patterns.rule: Use 'at this time' to refer to the present; 'don't need to' + base verb for lack of necessity.

patterns.en: I didn't think Tom was your type.
patterns.rule: Use past simple 'didn't think' for past thoughts; 'was' for past state.

patterns.en: I was busy.
patterns.rule: Use past simple 'was' for past state.

patterns.en: I'm proud of my work.
patterns.rule: Use 'be proud of' + noun to express satisfaction.

patterns.en: I didn't mean to hurt you.
patterns.rule: Use 'didn't mean to' + base verb to express unintentional actions.

patterns.en: Keep in mind that Tom doesn't speak French very well.
patterns.rule: Use 'keep in mind that' + clause to remind someone; present simple for habitual actions.

patterns.en: You make me laugh.
patterns.rule: Use 'make' + object + base verb to express causation.

patterns.en: I could do this myself.
patterns.rule: Use 'could' + base verb for past ability or tentative present ability.

patterns.en: That's something to think about.
patterns.rule: Use 'something to' + base verb to indicate a consideration.

patterns.en: All of a sudden, a dog began barking.
patterns.rule: Use 'all of a sudden' to indicate a sudden event; past simple 'began' for past actions.

patterns.en: In some ways, Boston is nicer than Chicago.
patterns.rule: Use 'in some ways' to express partial comparison; comparative 'nicer than' to compare two things.

patterns.en: It's good to see you smile.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's good to' + base verb to express pleasure at an action.

patterns.en: Let me help you with your suitcases.
patterns.rule: Use 'let me' + base verb to offer assistance.

patterns.en: I guess it was a joke.
patterns.rule: Use 'I guess' to express uncertainty; past simple 'was' for past events.

patterns.en: Not only can't I tell Tom, I can't even tell you.
patterns.rule: Use 'not only... but also' for emphasis; in spoken English, it's acceptable to use this structure without inversion.

patterns.en: I was a student at that time.
patterns.rule: Use past simple 'was' for past states; 'at that time' for time reference.

patterns.en: It's possible that Tom will get into Harvard.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's possible that' + clause to express possibility; 'will' + base verb for future actions.

patterns.en: I was surprised to find out that Tom had children.
patterns.rule: Use 'was surprised to' + base verb to express reactions; past perfect 'had' + past participle for earlier past events.

patterns.en: I wish I had a beautiful girlfriend.
patterns.rule: Use 'wish' + past simple to express desires about the present.

patterns.en: I doubt that Tom is guilty.
patterns.rule: Use 'doubt that' + clause to express disbelief; present simple 'is' for current state.

patterns.en: I'm here because I need your help.
patterns.rule: Use 'because' + clause to give reasons; 'need' + noun for necessity.

patterns.en: I'm aware of what's going on.
patterns.rule: Use 'be aware of' + noun clause to express knowledge of a situation.

patterns.en: It appears that he's a student.
patterns.rule: Use 'it appears that' + clause to express observations.

patterns.en: Don't be so selfish.
patterns.rule: Use imperative 'don't be' + adjective to advise against a behavior.

patterns.en: I still don't want to go.
patterns.rule: Use 'still' before the main verb to indicate that a situation hasn't changed.

patterns.en: I started studying French three years ago.
patterns.rule: Use past simple 'started' for past actions; 'verb-ing' after 'start' when referring to activities.

patterns.en: I told you it was a bad idea.
patterns.rule: Use past simple 'told' for past actions; 'it was' for past states.

patterns.en: I don't want to make any promises I can't keep.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't want to' + base verb to express desires not to do something; use relative clause 'I can't keep' to modify 'promises'.

patterns.en: I pretended that I didn't see it.
patterns.rule: Use past simple 'pretended' for past actions; 'didn't see' for past negative actions.

patterns.en: I didn't say this was my office.
patterns.rule: Use past simple 'didn't say' for past actions; 'this was' for past states.

patterns.en: I bought a camera the other day.
patterns.rule: Use 'the other day' to refer to a recent past; past simple 'bought' for completed actions.

patterns.en: It's important to follow a strict diet.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's important to' + base verb to express necessity or recommendations.

patterns.en: To tell the truth, I didn't do my homework.
patterns.rule: Use 'to tell the truth' to preface a confession; past simple 'didn't do' for past actions.

patterns.en: I'm dying to know what's inside.
patterns.rule: Use 'be dying to' + base verb to express eagerness; use contraction 'what's' for 'what is'.

patterns.en: That's one of my favorite books.
patterns.rule: Use 'that's' as contraction for 'that is'; possessive 'my' to indicate ownership.

patterns.en: I know I can do it.
patterns.rule: Use present simple 'know' for current knowledge; 'can' + base verb for ability.

patterns.en: I enjoy music.
patterns.rule: Use present simple to express likes; 'enjoy' + noun.

patterns.en: No matter what you say, I won't change my mind.
patterns.rule: Use 'no matter what' + clause to express that an action won't affect the outcome; 'won't' + base verb for future refusals.

patterns.en: Because of the rain, I could not go out.
patterns.rule: Use 'because of' + noun to give reasons; 'could not' + base verb for past inability.

patterns.en: Call me if something happens.
patterns.rule: Use 'if' + present simple for future conditions; imperative 'call me' for instructions.

patterns.en: There are a lot of books in the library.
patterns.rule: Use 'there are' with plural nouns to indicate existence; 'a lot of' to indicate large quantity.

patterns.en: I love cats.
patterns.rule: Use plural 'cats' to refer to the animal in general; present simple 'love' for strong liking.

patterns.en: I was up all night reading a book.
patterns.rule: Use 'was up all night' to indicate staying awake; 'verb-ing' after 'was' for past continuous actions.

patterns.en: I had a hard time finding his house.
patterns.rule: Use 'had a hard time' + verb-ing to express difficulty with an action.

patterns.en: Now that I'm here, everything's going to be okay.
patterns.rule: Use 'now that' + clause to indicate a change in circumstances; 'going to' + base verb for future predictions.

patterns.en: You need to call Tom immediately.
patterns.rule: Use 'need to' + base verb for necessity; 'immediately' as an adverb of time.

patterns.en: Before doing that, you need to ask Tom for permission.
patterns.rule: Use 'before' + verb-ing to indicate prior actions; 'need to' + base verb for necessity.

patterns.en: I make it a rule to get up early in the morning.
patterns.rule: Use 'make it a rule to' + base verb to express habitual actions; 'in the morning' for time reference.

patterns.en: Make sure the door is locked.
patterns.rule: Use imperative 'make sure' + clause to give instructions; 'is locked' as passive voice for state.

patterns.en: I'm having trouble understanding you.
patterns.rule: Use 'be having trouble' + verb-ing to express difficulty with an ongoing action.

patterns.en: I was amazed at Tom's fluency in French.
patterns.rule: Use 'was amazed at' + noun to express surprise; possessive 'Tom's'.

patterns.en: That's all I can tell you at this time.
patterns.rule: Use 'that's all' to indicate limitation; 'can' + base verb for ability.

patterns.en: I must go.
patterns.rule: Use 'must' + base verb to express necessity or obligation.

patterns.en: I'm satisfied with what I have.
patterns.rule: Use 'be satisfied with' + noun to express contentment.

patterns.en: I'll be right back.
patterns.rule: Use 'will' + base verb for future actions; 'right back' as an expression meaning 'soon'.

patterns.en: Don't make me say it twice.
patterns.rule: Use imperative 'don't make me' + base verb to express a strong request.

patterns.en: I can hardly walk.
patterns.rule: Use 'can hardly' + base verb to express difficulty performing an action.

patterns.en: You must be hungry.
patterns.rule: Use 'must be' + adjective to express a logical conclusion.

patterns.en: Even though it was raining, we decided to take a walk.
patterns.rule: Use 'even though' + clause to express contrast; past simple for past actions.

patterns.en: No sooner had it stopped raining than a beautiful rainbow appeared.
patterns.rule: Use 'no sooner... than...' with inversion ('had' + subject + past participle) to indicate immediate sequence.

patterns.en: Here is your book.
patterns.rule: Use 'here is' + singular noun; subject-verb inversion for emphasis.

patterns.en: I intend to stay in Boston for three days.
patterns.rule: Use 'intend to' + base verb to express plans; time expressions at the end.

patterns.en: Be careful not to cut yourself.
patterns.rule: Use imperative 'be careful not to' + base verb to give warnings.

patterns.en: I don't even know where my mother was born.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't even know' to emphasize ignorance; past simple 'was born' for past events.

patterns.en: Luckily, Tom had an extra umbrella.
patterns.rule: Use 'luckily' to express good fortune; past simple 'had' for past possession.

patterns.en: He's about the same age as you.
patterns.rule: Use 'as... as' to make comparisons of equality; 'you' without emphasis unless necessary.

patterns.en: I'm no longer afraid of you.
patterns.rule: Use 'no longer' to indicate that something has changed; contraction 'I'm' for 'I am'.

patterns.en: I also heard a similar story.
patterns.rule: Use 'also' before the main verb to add information; past simple tense for completed actions.

patterns.en: I believe I can help.
patterns.rule: Use 'can' to express ability; present simple tense for statements of belief.

patterns.en: All right, let's try it again.
patterns.rule: Use 'let's' to suggest an action; 'it' refers to the task being retried.

patterns.en: Every time I read this book, I find something new.
patterns.rule: Use present simple tense for habitual actions; 'this' as a demonstrative adjective.

patterns.en: The more you have, the more you want.
patterns.rule: Use 'the more... the more...' structure to show proportional relationships.

patterns.en: Don't forget your passport.
patterns.rule: Use the imperative form for commands; 'your' as a possessive adjective.

patterns.en: I accidentally spilled the milk.
patterns.rule: Use adverbs like 'accidentally' to modify verbs; past simple tense for past actions.

patterns.en: Listen, I'm really sorry.
patterns.rule: Use 'listen' to get someone's attention; 'I'm' as a contraction of 'I am'.

patterns.en: I'm grateful to you.
patterns.rule: Use 'grateful to' someone to express thanks.

patterns.en: I apologize for being late.
patterns.rule: Use 'apologize for' + verb-ing to express regret for an action.

patterns.en: I think that's a great idea.
patterns.rule: Use 'that's' as a contraction of 'that is'; present simple tense for opinions.

patterns.en: It's very unlikely that Tom will come.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's' for 'it is'; 'will' for future actions; 'unlikely' to express doubt.

patterns.en: As I told you before, I have no choice.
patterns.rule: Use past simple 'told' for past actions; 'have no choice' to express necessity.

patterns.en: I'm on my way to meet Tom at the station right now.
patterns.rule: Use 'on my way to' + base verb to indicate immediate plans; present continuous for current actions.

patterns.en: I'm planning to move back to Boston next year.
patterns.rule: Use 'planning to' + base verb for future intentions; time expressions at the end.

patterns.en: It has nothing to do with me.
patterns.rule: Use 'has nothing to do with' to indicate no connection.

patterns.en: So far, I've told no one.
patterns.rule: Use 'so far' with present perfect tense to indicate actions up to the present.

patterns.en: It's impossible to eat soup with a fork.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's' for 'it is'; 'impossible to' + base verb to express impracticality.

patterns.en: I've been here for three years.
patterns.rule: Use present perfect tense for actions that started in the past and continue now; 'for' + duration.

patterns.en: I don't have anything to eat.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't have' to express lack of possession; 'anything' in negative sentences.

patterns.en: I'm still in bed.
patterns.rule: Use 'still' to indicate continuation; present simple tense for current states.

patterns.en: Help me clean out the garage.
patterns.rule: Use the imperative mood for requests; 'clean out' as a phrasal verb meaning to empty completely.

patterns.en: You should ask Tom to help you.
patterns.rule: Use 'should' for advice; 'ask' someone 'to' + base verb.

patterns.en: I can't stop thinking about what they did to me.
patterns.rule: Use 'can't stop' + verb-ing to express an ongoing action that's hard to cease.

patterns.en: For all we know, Tom could be over 30.
patterns.rule: Use 'for all we know' to express uncertainty; 'could be' for possibility.

patterns.en: I was able to finish the work earlier than I had expected.
patterns.rule: Use 'was able to' for past abilities; comparative 'earlier than' for timing.

patterns.en: I couldn't find my keys.
patterns.rule: Use 'couldn't' as the past tense of 'can't' to express past inability.

patterns.en: I fell asleep while listening to the radio.
patterns.rule: Use 'while' + verb-ing for simultaneous actions in the past.

patterns.en: I didn't know him at the time.
patterns.rule: Use past simple tense for past states; 'at the time' for specific time reference.

patterns.en: For years, Tom suffered from migraine headaches.
patterns.rule: Use past simple tense for actions that occurred over a period in the past.

patterns.en: Find out what Tom knows.
patterns.rule: Use the imperative form for commands; 'find out' as a phrasal verb meaning to discover.

patterns.en: I don't have time to finish my homework.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't have time to' + base verb to express lack of time for an activity.

patterns.en: I've known Tom since high school.
patterns.rule: Use present perfect tense with 'since' to indicate when an action began.

patterns.en: All I have is a book.
patterns.rule: Use 'all I have is' to emphasize limited possession.

patterns.en: I have no intention of doing that today.
patterns.rule: Use 'have no intention of' + verb-ing to express unwillingness.

patterns.en: It didn't surprise me at all that Tom couldn't afford a lawyer.
patterns.rule: Use past simple tense; 'couldn't afford' for past inability.

patterns.en: It's my turn to take out the trash.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's my turn to' + base verb to indicate responsibility.

patterns.en: I'm willing to take that chance.
patterns.rule: Use 'be willing to' + base verb to express readiness or agreement.

patterns.en: The longer you wait to tell Tom, the harder it's going to be.
patterns.rule: Use 'the longer... the harder...' to show proportional relationships.

patterns.en: It's been a while since I've seen Tom.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's been a while since' + past simple for time elapsed since an action.

patterns.en: Let me know when you're ready.
patterns.rule: Use 'let me know' + clause to request notification.

patterns.en: It's obvious Tom doesn't like Mary.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's obvious' + clause to state clear facts.

patterns.en: Suddenly, it became noisy.
patterns.rule: Use 'suddenly' to indicate an abrupt change; past simple tense for past events.

patterns.en: It's hard to figure out who's telling the truth.
patterns.rule: Use 'figure out' as a phrasal verb meaning to understand; 'who's' for 'who is'.

patterns.en: I'm trying to figure out what's wrong.
patterns.rule: Use present continuous tense for actions happening now.

patterns.en: I was wondering if you were still here.
patterns.rule: Use 'was wondering' for polite past inquiries; past continuous tense.

patterns.en: I'm lucky to be here.
patterns.rule: Use 'lucky to be' + place to express gratitude for being somewhere.

patterns.en: I wonder how this works.
patterns.rule: Use 'I wonder how' + clause to express curiosity.

patterns.en: At this point, I don't need money.
patterns.rule: Use 'at this point' to refer to the current situation.

patterns.en: Let's clean up this mess.
patterns.rule: Use 'let's' for suggestions; 'clean up' as a phrasal verb.

patterns.en: I'm prepared to help Tom.
patterns.rule: Use 'prepared to' + base verb to express readiness.

patterns.en: I asked her if she had been to Mexico.
patterns.rule: Use past perfect 'had been' for actions completed before another past action.

patterns.en: You seem happy today.
patterns.rule: Use 'seem' + adjective to express appearance or perception.

patterns.en: According to the thermometer, it's 30 degrees outside.
patterns.rule: Use 'according to' to cite a source; 'it's' for 'it is'.

patterns.en: It never occurred to me that he might be an escaped prisoner.
patterns.rule: Use 'occurred to me' to express realization; past simple tense.

patterns.en: I was disappointed that you didn't call.
patterns.rule: Use 'was disappointed that' + clause to express feelings about a past event.

patterns.en: I have nothing to do.
patterns.rule: Use 'have nothing to do' to express boredom or lack of tasks.

patterns.en: I barely know her.
patterns.rule: Use 'barely' to indicate minimal acquaintance; present simple tense.

patterns.en: I had a feeling you would be late.
patterns.rule: Use 'had a feeling' to express intuition about a past event.

patterns.en: Frankly speaking, this novel isn't very interesting.
patterns.rule: Use 'frankly speaking' to preface an honest opinion.

patterns.en: I already told Tom everything.
patterns.rule: Use 'already' with past simple for actions completed before now.

patterns.en: I was impressed by Tom's courage.
patterns.rule: Use 'impressed by' to express admiration; possessive 'Tom's'.

patterns.en: Tell me what you know about the incident.
patterns.rule: Use imperative form for requests; 'what you know' as an object clause.

patterns.en: It's okay to make a couple of mistakes.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's okay to' + base verb to express permission or acceptance.

patterns.en: To make matters worse, it began to rain.
patterns.rule: Use 'to make matters worse' to indicate an additional problem.

patterns.en: I'm sorry for my terrible French; I'm still a beginner.
patterns.rule: Use a semicolon to connect related independent clauses.

patterns.en: I certainly don't mind helping you.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't mind' + verb-ing to express willingness.

patterns.en: It doesn't bother me if you take that book.
patterns.rule: Use 'it doesn't bother me' to express indifference; conditional 'if'.

patterns.en: At last, the baby fell asleep.
patterns.rule: Use 'at last' to express relief; past simple tense.

patterns.en: I don't consider myself to be good-looking.
patterns.rule: Use 'consider myself to be' + adjective for self-assessment.

patterns.en: I'm certain that you saw Tom.
patterns.rule: Use 'certain that' to express strong belief.

patterns.en: I've been studying French for three years.
patterns.rule: Use present perfect continuous tense for ongoing actions.

patterns.en: I can't help thinking about Tom.
patterns.rule: Use 'can't help' + verb-ing to express an uncontrollable action.

patterns.en: In retrospect, Tom wishes he had spent more time studying.
patterns.rule: Use 'wishes he had' + past participle to express regret about the past.

patterns.en: I don't understand what this sentence means.
patterns.rule: Use present simple tense for current understanding.

patterns.en: The last time I saw him, he was very healthy.
patterns.rule: Use past simple for actions; past continuous for states at that time.

patterns.en: I demand to know what's going on here.
patterns.rule: Use 'demand to' + base verb to express insistence.

patterns.en: As soon as she saw me, she started to cry.
patterns.rule: Use 'as soon as' for immediate sequences in the past.

patterns.en: For now, Tom can stay here.
patterns.rule: Use 'for now' to indicate a temporary situation; 'can' for permission.

patterns.en: I ought to have attended the lecture.
patterns.rule: Use 'ought to have' + past participle for past obligations not met.

patterns.en: It'll likely take much longer than you expect.
patterns.rule: Use 'likely' to express probability; comparative 'longer than'.

patterns.en: I promise you I'll never leave you.
patterns.rule: Use 'promise' + object + future tense for assurances.

patterns.en: As strange as it may sound, what Tom said is true.
patterns.rule: Use 'as... as' for comparisons; present simple tense for facts.

patterns.en: That's what I was looking for.
patterns.rule: Use 'was looking for' in past continuous to express ongoing past actions.

patterns.en: I have something I need to do.
patterns.rule: Use 'have something' + relative clause to specify tasks.

patterns.en: It's dangerous to climb a mountain during a storm.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's dangerous to' + base verb to express risk.

patterns.en: I come from a long line of doctors.
patterns.rule: Use 'come from' to indicate origin; 'a long line of' for ancestry.

patterns.en: I'm busy getting ready for my trip.
patterns.rule: Use 'busy' + verb-ing to indicate current activities.

patterns.en: Except for Tom, I didn't know anyone there.
patterns.rule: Use 'except for' to exclude; past simple tense for past events.

patterns.en: Come to my office anytime.
patterns.rule: Use the imperative mood for invitations; 'anytime' as an indefinite time.

patterns.en: I've known Tom for almost 10 years.
patterns.rule: Use present perfect tense with 'for' + duration.

patterns.en: I'm thrilled to be back.
patterns.rule: Use 'thrilled to be' + place to express excitement.

patterns.en: I'm sorry to cause you all this trouble.
patterns.rule: Use 'sorry to' + base verb to apologize for actions.

patterns.en: I'm working on my speech.
patterns.rule: Use present continuous tense for ongoing tasks.

patterns.en: I can't put up with this noise anymore.
patterns.rule: Use 'can't put up with' + noun to express intolerance.

patterns.en: I'm starting to get used to living here.
patterns.rule: Use 'get used to' + verb-ing to express acclimation.

patterns.en: Generally speaking, boys can run faster than girls.
patterns.rule: Use 'generally speaking' for general statements; comparative 'faster than'.

patterns.en: I wish I had studied French when I was in high school.
patterns.rule: Use 'wish' + past perfect to express regret about the past.

patterns.en: It's still not ready.
patterns.rule: Use 'still' before the verb to indicate continuation; present simple tense for current states.

patterns.en: Were you busy?
patterns.rule: Use past simple 'were' for past states; question form for past inquiries.

patterns.en: Which one would you choose?
patterns.rule: Use 'which one' to ask for a choice; 'would' for hypothetical situations.

patterns.en: Don't go anywhere, okay?
patterns.rule: Use imperative 'don't' + base verb for negative commands; 'okay?' seeks confirmation.

patterns.en: How am I supposed to do this by myself?
patterns.rule: Use 'am I supposed to' + base verb to express confusion about expectations.

patterns.en: Exactly what kind of work do you do?
patterns.rule: Use 'exactly' for emphasis; present simple for occupations.

patterns.en: Do you mind if I open the window?
patterns.rule: Use 'do you mind if' + subject + present tense verb for polite requests.

patterns.en: Is there any place around here where we can get something to eat?
patterns.rule: Use 'is there' to inquire about existence; 'where we can get something to eat' as a relative clause.

patterns.en: What made her do that?
patterns.rule: Use 'what made' + object + base verb to ask about reasons; past tense 'made'.

patterns.en: Exactly how much money was stolen?
patterns.rule: Use 'exactly' for precision; past passive 'was stolen' for completed actions.

patterns.en: Don't you have friends?
patterns.rule: Use negative question to express surprise; present simple for states.

patterns.en: About how long will it take?
patterns.rule: Use 'about' for approximation; 'will' for future predictions.

patterns.en: What more do I need?
patterns.rule: Use 'what more' to ask about additional requirements; present simple tense.

patterns.en: When are we leaving?
patterns.rule: Use 'when are we' + verb-ing for future plans; present continuous tense.

patterns.en: What are you cooking today?
patterns.rule: Use present continuous 'are you cooking' for near-future actions.

patterns.en: How's the weather where you are?
patterns.rule: Use contraction 'how's' for 'how is'; 'where you are' specifies location.

patterns.en: How was the food?
patterns.rule: Use past simple 'was' to ask about past experiences.

patterns.en: How tall is the Eiffel Tower?

patterns.en: Have you finished writing that song you've been working on?

patterns.en: Would it be okay if I didn't invite Tom to my party?

patterns.en: Do you have any idea what Tom wants?

patterns.en: What would happen if I push this button?

patterns.en: Exactly how does this work?

patterns.en: How did Tom do that?

patterns.en: How long can you hold your breath?

patterns.en: How long was Tom here yesterday?

patterns.en: Is it hard to learn French?

patterns.en: Perhaps it will rain tomorrow.

patterns.en: It's already open.

patterns.en: There's no need to worry about Tom.

patterns.en: One of the doors was broken.
patterns.rule: Use 'one of the' + plural noun; past passive 'was broken' for past states.

patterns.en: He accidentally shot himself in the foot while cleaning his gun.
patterns.rule: Use past simple tense for past actions; 'while' + verb-ing for simultaneous actions.

patterns.en: All you need to do is remember these three very simple steps.
patterns.rule: Use 'all you need to do is' + base verb to emphasize simplicity; adjectives modify 'steps'.

patterns.en: Tom goes to the same school as I do.
patterns.rule: Use present simple for habitual actions; 'as I do' for comparison.

patterns.en: There must be a way we can convince Tom to work for us.
patterns.rule: Use 'must' to express necessity; 'convince' as the base verb.

patterns.en: Let Tom do that for you.
patterns.rule: Use 'let' + object + base verb to allow someone to perform an action.

patterns.en: Tom looks like he wants to say something.
patterns.rule: Use 'looks like' + clause to express appearance or impression.

patterns.en: This is probably the key that Tom is looking for.
patterns.rule: Use 'probably' for likelihood; relative clause 'that Tom is looking for' modifies 'key'.

patterns.en: Tom asked me why I was here.
patterns.rule: Use indirect questions; maintain past tense consistency after 'asked'.

patterns.en: This is the first time I've ever written a letter in French.
patterns.rule: Use present perfect tense for experiences up to now; capitalize 'French'.

patterns.en: Look at the picture on the wall.
patterns.rule: Use imperative mood for commands; prepositional phrase 'on the wall' indicates location.

patterns.en: Tom says that he knows you.
patterns.rule: Use present simple for reporting speech; 'that' can be omitted in informal contexts.

patterns.en: Let's do this before it gets hot.
patterns.rule: Use 'let's' for suggestions; 'before' introduces a time clause.

patterns.en: Put on this sweater.
patterns.rule: Use 'put on' as a separable phrasal verb meaning 'to dress in'; imperative mood.

patterns.en: Let's concentrate on what needs to be done today.
patterns.rule: Use 'let's' + base verb for suggestions; 'what needs to be done' is a noun clause.

patterns.en: I agree with you on that point.
patterns.rule: Use 'agree with' + person; 'on that point' specifies the subject of agreement.

patterns.en: Tom reluctantly handed Mary the money.
patterns.rule: Use adverbs like 'reluctantly' to express manner; indirect object before direct object.

patterns.en: Almost everyone I know has a bicycle.
patterns.rule: Use 'almost everyone' as a singular subject; 'has' for third-person singular.

patterns.en: Tom asked me what I wanted.
patterns.rule: Use past simple in reported speech after a past tense verb; 'wanted' matches 'asked'.

patterns.en: Tom already knows what happened.
patterns.rule: Use present simple for current knowledge; 'already' indicates prior awareness.

patterns.en: Tom waited for Mary to come home.
patterns.rule: Use 'waited for' + object + 'to' + base verb; past simple tense.

patterns.en: There's someone outside.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; 'someone' as an indefinite pronoun.

patterns.en: Tom was wearing a gray suit and a red tie.
patterns.rule: Use past continuous for past actions in progress; adjectives describe nouns.

patterns.en: Tom was unable to find Mary a good job.
patterns.rule: Use 'was unable to' + base verb to express inability in the past.

patterns.en: Clean up your room.
patterns.rule: Use imperative mood for commands; 'clean up' as a phrasal verb.

patterns.en: Come and see for yourself.
patterns.rule: Use imperative 'come and see'; 'for yourself' emphasizes personal experience.

patterns.en: I could have helped you with your work.
patterns.rule: Use 'could have' + past participle to express an unfulfilled past ability.

patterns.en: It's quite likely that Tom will come.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's' for 'it is'; 'quite likely' expresses a strong possibility.

patterns.en: I called Tom from the hospital.
patterns.rule: Use past simple for completed actions; prepositional phrase 'from the hospital'.

patterns.en: This is the way he learned English.
patterns.rule: Use 'this is the way' to introduce a method; capitalize 'English'.

patterns.en: Tom realized it was useless to argue.
patterns.rule: Use 'realized' in past simple; 'it was useless to' + base verb expresses futility.

patterns.en: Tom apologized to Mary for being late.
patterns.rule: Use 'apologized to' + person; 'for' + verb-ing to explain the reason.

patterns.en: All we need is a little more practice.
patterns.rule: Use 'all we need is' + noun phrase to express necessities.

patterns.en: Let's try to treat each other with respect.
patterns.rule: Use 'let's' for inclusive suggestions; 'each other' as a reciprocal pronoun.

patterns.en: All we want is information.
patterns.rule: Use 'all we want is' + noun to express desires or requirements.

patterns.en: There's really no reason for you to come to Boston.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; 'no reason for' + object + 'to' + base verb.

patterns.en: Let me introduce you to my beautiful wife.
patterns.rule: Use 'let me' + base verb for offers; 'introduce' + object + 'to' someone.

patterns.en: I don't care who Tom talks to.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't care' + question word + clause to express indifference.

patterns.en: I asked for their approval.

patterns.en: Tom filled the room with cardboard boxes.

patterns.en: Tom asked me to open the window.
patterns.rule: Use 'asked' + object + 'to' + base verb for requests.

patterns.en: Let's go to the theater early so we can get good seats.
patterns.rule: Use 'so we can' to express purpose; 'let's' for suggestions.

patterns.en: Tom wondered when the meeting would start.

patterns.en: Tom speaks French like a native speaker.

patterns.en: Tom asked Mary to give him a kiss.
patterns.rule: Use 'asked' + object + 'to' + base verb; indirect object 'him'.

patterns.en: Tom was the last one to get here.

patterns.en: This is why I quit the job.

patterns.en: This is so good.

patterns.rule: Use 'gave' + indirect object + direct object; 'useful' modifies 'advice'.

patterns.en: This is where I brought my girlfriend on our first date.

patterns.en: There seems to be a mistake.

patterns.en: I don't care what Tom did.

patterns.en: Tom was here too.
patterns.rule: Use 'too' to indicate addition; past simple 'was' for past states.

patterns.en: Everything is okay.

patterns.en: Tom talked Mary into donating some money.
patterns.rule: Use 'talked... into' + verb-ing to indicate persuasion.

patterns.en: The most important thing you can do now is to remain calm.
patterns.rule: Use infinitive 'to remain' after 'is' for actions; 'most important' as a superlative.

patterns.en: Tell me about your trip to Boston.
patterns.rule: Use imperative mood for requests; preposition 'to' indicates destination.

patterns.en: This is the place where Tom met Mary.
patterns.rule: Use relative clause 'where Tom met Mary' to modify 'place'.

patterns.en: I don't care if you like me or not.
patterns.rule: Use 'if... or not' to cover both possibilities; express indifference.

patterns.en: Tom can't afford to buy a new bicycle.
patterns.rule: Use 'can't afford to' + base verb to express financial limitations.

patterns.en: The best way to learn a language is to live in a country where it's spoken.

patterns.en: Tom should be there by 2:30.

patterns.en: Tom forgot to feed Mary's dog.

patterns.en: Allow me to introduce myself.

patterns.en: Choose any dress you like.

patterns.en: Tell me how to do it.
patterns.rule: Use 'tell me' + question word + infinitive for instructions.

patterns.en: Tom wondered where Mary had spent the weekend.
patterns.rule: Use past perfect 'had spent' for actions before another past point.

patterns.en: Tom wished Mary were with him.
patterns.rule: Use subjunctive 'were' after 'wished' for unreal situations.

patterns.en: Tom came here to ask us to help him.
patterns.rule: Use infinitive of purpose; 'to ask' and 'to help'.

patterns.en: Tom had to go home early today.
patterns.rule: Use 'had to' + base verb to express past obligation.

patterns.en: Don't waste your time trying to convince Tom.

patterns.en: Tom seems very sleepy.

patterns.en: You look like a million bucks.

patterns.en: There's a lot of traffic here in the mornings.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; 'a lot of' indicates quantity.

patterns.en: It's actually a good idea.
patterns.rule: Use 'actually' to affirm or correct a perception.

patterns.en: Tom said he couldn't loan any money to Mary.
patterns.rule: Use past simple for reported speech; 'couldn't' as past inability.

patterns.en: Everybody's in bed.
patterns.rule: Contraction 'everybody's' for 'everybody is'; singular verb agreement.

patterns.en: Tom stopped talking when Mary came into the room.
patterns.rule: Use past simple for sequential past events; 'when' introduces a time clause.

patterns.en: Tom still has no idea what's going on.
patterns.rule: Use 'still' to indicate continuation; 'what's going on' as a noun clause.

patterns.en: Tom was a troubled child.
patterns.rule: Use 'was' for past states; adjective 'troubled' describes 'child'.

patterns.en: This is the only way I know how to do this.

patterns.en: It's fun to ride a motorcycle.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's' for 'it is'; infinitive 'to ride' expresses activity.

patterns.en: All you can do is trust one another.
patterns.rule: Use 'all... is' + base verb; 'one another' as reciprocal pronoun.

patterns.en: There's something wrong with my computer.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; 'something wrong with' indicates a problem.

patterns.en: Tom believes that unicorns are real.

patterns.en: You should think about it first.

patterns.en: This is such a waste of time.
patterns.rule: Use 'such a' + noun phrase for emphasis.

patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; 'I need to do' as a relative clause.

patterns.en: I can only speak French and a little English.

patterns.en: Tom should know this already.

patterns.en: Tom persuaded Mary to go to Boston with him.

patterns.en: All you ever think about is work.
patterns.rule: Use 'all... is' + noun; 'ever' emphasizes frequency.

patterns.en: Tom was the only one who saw Mary sneak into the room.
patterns.rule: Use relative clause 'who saw Mary sneak...'; past simple tense.

patterns.en: Tom hates shots.

patterns.en: There's nothing else to talk about.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; 'nothing else' indicates no further topics.

patterns.en: Don't leave your glasses on the table.
patterns.rule: Use imperative mood for commands; prepositional phrase indicates location.

patterns.en: Tom might be able to do that, but I doubt it.
patterns.rule: Use 'might be able to' for possibility; 'I doubt it' expresses skepticism.

patterns.en: There's no time for explanations.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; 'no time for' + noun.

patterns.en: Come back to the house.
patterns.rule: Use imperative mood; 'to the house' indicates destination.

patterns.en: It's rather cold for April.
patterns.rule: Use 'rather' for moderate emphasis; 'for April' sets a comparison.

patterns.en: No matter where you go, I'll follow you.

patterns.en: Tom sometimes appears on TV.
patterns.rule: Use 'sometimes' as an adverb of frequency; 'on TV' specifies medium.

patterns.en: Don't call me when I'm at the office.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't' for negative commands; 'when' introduces a time clause.

patterns.en: Tom spends way too much time playing games.
patterns.rule: Use 'way too much' for emphasis on excess; 'playing' as gerund.

patterns.en: That's a good picture of you.
patterns.rule: Use 'of you' to specify the subject in the picture.

patterns.en: I became friends with him while I was in Taiwan.

patterns.en: There's no reason to get upset.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; infinitive 'to get' expresses purpose.

patterns.en: There's a very good chance it was Tom who did that.

patterns.en: There's no way we can get this done.

patterns.en: Tom blames Mary for everything.

patterns.en: There's so much I want to show you.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; 'so much' indicates a large amount.

patterns.en: There's a chance Tom will be late.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; 'will be' for future possibility.

patterns.en: Tom asked Mary not to leave him alone.
patterns.rule: Use 'asked' + object + 'not to' + base verb for requests.

patterns.en: Don't worry about the results of your test.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't' + base verb for negative commands; 'about' introduces the object.

patterns.en: The person who donated this money wishes to remain anonymous.
patterns.rule: Use relative clause 'who donated...'; infinitive 'to remain' expresses intent.

patterns.en: It's definitely good news.
patterns.rule: Use 'definitely' for emphasis; 'good news' as a singular noun.

patterns.en: You'd better get back to class.
patterns.rule: Use 'you'd better' + base verb for strong advice.

patterns.en: All you have to do is push this button.
patterns.rule: Use 'all you have to do is' + base verb to express simplicity.

patterns.en: Tom asked Mary for her telephone number.
patterns.rule: Use 'asked' + object + 'for' + noun to request information.

patterns.en: Tom definitely had enough time to get the job done.
patterns.rule: Use 'definitely' for certainty; 'had' in past simple tense.

patterns.en: Bring your children with you.
patterns.rule: Use imperative mood for instructions; 'with you' indicates accompaniment.

patterns.en: Tom asked Mary where she wanted to go for lunch.
patterns.rule: Use indirect question format; past tense 'wanted' after 'asked'.

patterns.en: Let us know when you'll be coming to Boston.
patterns.rule: Use 'let us know' + 'when' clause; future continuous 'you'll be coming'.

patterns.en: Tom almost never watches TV.
patterns.rule: Use 'almost never' as an adverb of frequency; present simple tense.

patterns.en: Close the window, will you?
patterns.rule: Use tag questions for emphasis or politeness; imperative mood.

patterns.en: Tom actually likes Mary.
patterns.rule: Use 'actually' to indicate truth contrary to expectations.

patterns.en: Tom made it clear that he didn't like the food.
patterns.rule: Use 'made it clear that' + clause to express clarity in statements.

patterns.en: None of us like Tom.
patterns.rule: Use 'none of' + plural noun; verb agrees with plural noun in informal usage.

patterns.en: Don't be afraid to ask questions.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't be afraid to' + base verb to encourage action.

patterns.en: Get out of the water.
patterns.rule: Use imperative mood; 'get out of' as a phrasal verb meaning 'leave'.

patterns.en: Tom offered to feed my cat while I was out of town.

patterns.en: Tom asked me whether I liked Mary or not.

patterns.en: Tom kept on making the same mistake.

patterns.en: Tom really wants to be your friend.

patterns.en: It's kind of you to say that.

patterns.en: Tom asked Mary if he could kiss her.

patterns.en: It's quite delicious.
patterns.rule: Use 'quite' to moderately intensify an adjective.

patterns.en: Tom plans to live in Boston for more than a year.
patterns.rule: Use 'plans to' + base verb for future intentions; specify duration.

patterns.en: There's no place to hide.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; infinitive 'to hide' indicates purpose.

patterns.en: Tom barely made it in time.

patterns.en: Don't talk about people behind their backs.

patterns.en: Tom decided to tell Mary the truth.
patterns.rule: Use 'decided to' + base verb to express a choice.

patterns.en: Tom usually sleeps in this room.

patterns.en: Tell me why I'm here.
patterns.rule: Use imperative mood; 'why I'm here' as a noun clause.

patterns.en: Tom knew exactly what Mary meant.
patterns.rule: Use 'knew' in past simple; 'exactly' emphasizes precision.

patterns.en: Tom pretended that he couldn't speak French.
patterns.rule: Use 'pretended that' + clause; 'couldn't' as past ability.

patterns.en: Tom promised Mary that he wouldn't be late.

patterns.en: Enjoy your vacation.
patterns.rule: Use imperative mood for wishes or commands.

patterns.en: There used to be a prison here.

patterns.en: Keep your hands clean.
patterns.rule: Use imperative mood; 'keep' + object + adjective.

patterns.en: Keep an eye on the girls.

patterns.en: It was pretty expensive.

patterns.en: Tell me who I have to talk to.

patterns.en: Tom probably thought I was at school.

patterns.en: This is one of the best schools in the city.

patterns.en: I don't care which choice you make.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't care' + question word + clause to express indifference.

patterns.en: All you do is criticize others.

patterns.en: Tom asked Mary what kind of movies she liked.

patterns.en: Tom wondered who Mary was waiting for.

patterns.en: Tom accepted the gift.

patterns.en: Tom died of old age.

patterns.en: Tom wanted Mary to tell him her phone number.

patterns.en: Tom abandoned the idea of buying a new truck.

patterns.en: Tom went on eating.

patterns.en: Get me a towel.

patterns.en: Tom kept me waiting for more than 30 minutes.
patterns.rule: Use 'kept' + object + verb-ing to show someone caused another to continue an action; 'more than' indicates duration.

patterns.en: It took me three hours to write the letter.
patterns.rule: Use 'it took' + person + time + 'to' + base verb to express how long an action lasted.

patterns.en: This is quite new to me.
patterns.rule: Use 'quite' to mean 'fairly' or 'completely'; 'to me' shows personal relation.

patterns.en: Try to read as many books as possible.
patterns.rule: Use 'as many... as possible' to encourage maximizing quantity; imperative mood.

patterns.en: There's almost no milk left in the glass.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; 'almost no' indicates scarcity.

patterns.en: Tom almost always wears dark clothes.
patterns.rule: Use 'almost always' as an adverb of frequency; present simple for habits.

patterns.en: It's very dusty in here.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's' for 'it is'; 'in here' specifies location; 'very' intensifies 'dusty'.

patterns.en: There's only one place Tom is likely to hide.
patterns.rule: Use 'there's' for 'there is'; 'is likely to' expresses probability.

patterns.en: Remember what I told you.
patterns.rule: Use imperative mood; 'what I told you' is a noun clause acting as the object.

patterns.en: It's worth talking about.
patterns.rule: Use 'it's worth' + verb-ing to indicate that an action has value.

patterns.en: Let's go back to the hotel.
patterns.rule: Use 'let's' for suggestions; 'go back' is a phrasal verb meaning 'return'.

patterns.en: Don't ask me to explain it.
patterns.rule: Use 'don't' + base verb for negative commands; 'to explain' is the infinitive form.

patterns.en: Let's continue the game after supper.
patterns.rule: Use 'let's' for suggestions; 'after supper' specifies when.

patterns.en: Tom enjoys watching sports on TV.
patterns.rule: Use 'enjoys' + verb-ing for likes; 'on TV' specifies medium.

patterns.en: There are a lot of things for us to think about.
patterns.rule: Use 'there are' with plural nouns; 'to think about' is an infinitive phrase expressing purpose.
